question: Can one root-stub model execute cleanly across both the preserved GC-ISS split set and GC-PRB-0001, or must the preserved subset split into a narrower pilot?

commonModel.summary: The same stub shape can describe both single-successor ISS records and the multi-successor PRB umbrella, but the current execution-readiness differs across the two families.

reasons: All five records share the same single-successor redirect shape established by the ISS split package.
All five records are already treated uniformly as preserved legacy redirects in the first cleanup boundary.
None of the five records carries a paired support-only backfill body that would need synchronized relocation judgment.
The umbrella redirects to two current successors rather than one, so its stub wording and reader expectations are more loaded than the ISS pattern.
GC-PRB-0001 remains the canonical deprecated sample in early registry-model surfaces, not just a routine split redirect.
The umbrella still sits beside an already-moved support-only backfill note, so execution judgment should consider the pair explicitly instead of piggybacking on the ISS pilot.

p3Conclusion.nextRecommendedPilot: GC-ISS-* as one narrower first pilot package; keep GC-PRB-0001 out of that first execution round.
stopReasonsForFullSubsetMove: multi-successor umbrella handling not yet defended for PRB execution
canonical deprecated sample role still live on PRB in early registry-history surfaces
paired umbrella plus support-only-backfill relationship should be judged explicitly rather than folded into the ISS pilot
